patches.purpose: SSE batch flush (20 frames / 30ms idle) — cut per-frame enqueue+stringify overhead under high event volume; renderer messages were trickling after task completion
patches.note: 2026-08-22 applied to running kernel. Backup .bak-sse-batch-20260822. Marker 'BATCH_MAX = 20' in sseResponse. A0 2026-09-10: source .bak not present in install tree (verified absent) -> sourceBroken; A1 will reverse-build the diff from the current installed file vs official @0.1.1-rc.2. See apiproxySequence. verifyfix 2026-09-10: v205 retarget to dsh-api-gateway/lib/index.js (BATCH_MAX = 20 present); rc.2 path kept in rc2Target. | v209 2026-09-11 rewrite: original sseResponse BATCH_MAX=20 landing did not survive the 0.1.5 gateway refactor as-is — rebased onto RemoteStreamMuxConnection write chain (WRITE_BATCH_MAX=20 / 30ms idle / 1MiB high-water backpressure, consts @270-279, flushBatch @375-389, drainBuffered @416-418). Verify anchor 'BATCH_MAX = 20' still hits (substring of WRITE_BATCH_MAX = 20 @275).
patches.v209: deliberately not ported. The 0.2.0 gateway speaks WebSocket, where the protocol is strictly one frame per message with an exactKeys check — there is no batching primitive to hook, so the 0.1.5 "20 frames / 30ms idle" flush has no equivalent here. Not drift: a recorded decision.
patches.portNote: Re-checked on 0.2.0 and the earlier "no cost to amortise" claim was WRONG. The SSE writer is gone, but the WebSocket writer still costs one JSON.stringify + one socket.send + one promise per message (dsh-api-gateway/lib/types/stream-server.js send()). The promise chain fixes ordering and back-pressure, not the per-frame cost. It cannot be batched as written: parseRemoteStreamClientMessage parses EXACTLY ONE message per text with strict exactKeys validation, so joining frames would break the protocol on the client side. Porting needs a batch message type on both ends - a protocol change, not a patch. Context for the cost: the per-frame cost is lower than the SSE path P13 was written against (already-stringified text, no controller.enqueue, no re-encode), so this is a regression risk rather than a known outage.

patches.purpose: An OpenAI-compatible relay that loses its upstream answers HTTP 200 with content-type text/event-stream and puts the failure inside the stream as an in-band `data: {...,"error":{"code":502,"message":"JSON error injected into SSE stream","metadata":{"error_type":"provider_unavailable"}}}`. pi-ai keeps only error.message, so the status code and error_type never reach classifyPiAiError, and the bare text matched none of its rules — it fell through to the catch-all PI_AI_ERROR. PI_AI_ERROR is absent from DEFAULT_RETRYABLE_CODES (dsh-llm), so dsh-llm-retry returned next() and killed the turn on the first transient blip regardless of the provider retryPolicy.maxRetries. The rule classifies the relay wording as SERVER, the class the dropped 502 would have received.
patches.note: Registered 2026-09-30 from session-1363ee2e-2a8c-4a05-a566-a964477a5cc2, which failed turn 4 and turn 5 back to back with PI_AI_ERROR at 0/0/0 usage while basic-compaction-engine logged "Connection error." twice in the same 16s window. The relay was probed directly and reproduced the in-band error on demand (POST /chat/completions with an unsupported role returns 200 text/event-stream carrying {"error":{"code":502,"message":"JSON error injected into SSE stream","metadata":{"error_type":"provider_unavailable"}}}), and the same real 111k-token context from that session then completed normally, so the payload was not at fault. Verified with scripts/test-p41-classify.mjs: 18/18 including three negative controls that must stay PI_AI_ERROR (stream ended pending, deferred response, unrelated text).
patches.discovered_by: host log dsh-2026-09-30 PI_AI_ERROR + direct replay against https://api.commandcode.ai/provider/v1/chat/completions

patches.purpose: removeScoped called fiber.dispose().catch(...). Fiber.dispose() is synchronous in cordis 4 — it returns void, which is why cordis wraps its own call sites in Promise.resolve — so the bare .catch threw TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'catch') on every agent disposal. The throw escaped the agent/disposed listener, so the disposal diagnostic the sink was written to log was never emitted and the remaining disposed listeners in the chain were cut short.
patches.note: Registered 2026-09-30. The host log carries this TypeError 10 times on 2026-09-30 across five distinct sessions, each immediately preceded by `session-projection-cache ... turn/end write ... failed (cache stays stale): SessionHandleClosedError: flush on a closed handle`, i.e. a session closed while its turn was still ending. Verified with scripts/test-p42-dispose.mjs, which pins the real cordis-4 shape (dispose() -> undefined) and fails if the old call site stops throwing.
patches.discovered_by: host log dsh-2026-09-30 agent-registry listener-throw + cordis 4 dispose contract read from cordis/lib/index.js:1123

patches.purpose: Normalise the tool_call ids this process mints before the request leaves for the provider. Some OpenAI-compatible relays refuse a replayed assistant turn whose parallel tool_calls carry hyphenated ids and report it as HTTP 200 with an in-band `data: {...,"error":{...}}` chunk rather than a readable status, so the client sees the opaque `PI_AI_ERROR: JSON error injected into SSE stream` on the first attempt and the turn dies. With the ids rewritten the same request is accepted.
patches.note: Registered 2026-09-30 for session-1363ee2e-2a8c-4a05-a566-a964477a5cc2, which failed turns 4, 5 and 6 back to back at 0/0/0 usage. Scope measured, not guessed: with name, arguments, content and message shape held constant, seven neutral 32-char id shapes were accepted 4/4 each on api.commandcode.ai while the real `chatcmpl-tool-*` ids were refused 0/4; id length (8..40), character class, underscores and word+digit mixes were all irrelevant, which is why the rewrite is anchored to this process's own minting format rather than to a character class. IMPORTANT: the underlying reason the relay rejects them is still unknown - this makes the request acceptable, it does not explain the relay. Scoped to /^chatcmpl-/ so ids the model returns pass through untouched and the rewrite is one-shot per history rather than repeating every turn. The mapping is built once per request and applied to BOTH the assistant toolCall id and the toolResult toolCallId, because the relay pairs a result with its call by id; renaming one side only would orphan every result. Verified by scripts/test-p43-id-rewrite.mjs: 17/17 including pairing, idempotence, foreign-id passthrough and degenerate inputs.
patches.discovered_by: controlled replay of the exact payload DSH builds, cross-checked across commandcode/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash, yzs/u2-flash and bai/glm-5.3-flash (all 3/3-6/6 accept it), which ruled out the payload, the conversation data and the relay itself

patches.purpose: The Agent Team tool installer registers a REQUIRED systemPrompt context (team:identity) whose text() calls ctx.agentTeams.membership(agent). maybeInstall() guards on tryMembership at agent/created time, but a subagent/descriptor child has no descriptor yet at that moment, so the tools get installed; by the first step the descriptor exists, tryMembership returns undefined and membership() throws TEAM_NOT_MEMBER - killing every child turn of ANY subagent provider (routed, spawn, fork).
patches.note: Fix makes the identity text resolve non-throwing: tryMembership() and a neutral "delegated subagent, Team features unavailable" string when there is no membership. Behaviour for Leads and roster teammates is byte-identical. Verified: routed child turn no longer throws; node --check clean; patch applies to pristine (@dsh-experimental-tool-agent-team 0.2.1-rc.2).
patches.discovered_by: host log dsh-2026-10-20 TeamError stack: dsh-experimental-tool-agent-team:244 text() -> ctx.agentTeams.membership(agent) -> TeamRoster.membership:862

patches.purpose: spawnAdmitted() builds the child activation request as { prompt, parent } and drops every routing field, so a teammate started on a preset-mounting provider (routed-mount / routed-fork) cannot mount a preset: startLocal() reads agentPresetOf(request) for both childSessionMeta and composition.agentPreset. Forward request.agentPreset so team members honour the preset the caller asked for.
patches.note: One-line passthrough (plus comment) inside the request literal. Without it the hybrid model degrades to "teammate mounts the parent composition", which defeats the routed plugin core capability. Verified: node --check clean; patch applies to pristine (@dsh-experimental-agent-team 0.2.1-rc.2). Caller-side: dsh-routed-subagent team:true passes agentPreset.
patches.discovered_by: reading dsh-subagent startLocal(): L1484 childSessionMeta(..., agentPresetOf(request)) + L1490 composition:{agentPreset:agentPresetOf(request)} against the team service request literal
